exposure: Induction of labor at 40-40(+ 6) weeks' gestation
Induction of labor at 41-41(+ 6) weeks' gestation
outcome: Non-reassuring fetal heart rate patterns (as indication for CS)
Meconium-stained amniotic fluid (as indication for CS)
Failed induction of labor (as indication for CS)
cohort: A total of 603 low-risk women with singleton pregnancies undergoing induction of labor were included in the study.
finding: Induction of labor at 40 weeks resulted in a significantly lower cesarean section rate (25.1%) compared to IOL at 41 weeks (33.7%), with no significant differences in rates of neonatal asphyxia or NICU admission.
mod_finding: Induction of labor at 40 weeks resulted in a lower rate of cesarean section compared to IOL at 41 weeks, and parity >= 1 and a Bishop score >= 6 were identified as protective factors against cesarean section following IOL.
gest_age: Term pregnancies; induction of labor performed at 40-40(+ 6) weeks or 41-41(+ 6) weeks of gestation.
